objects.text: Simplified coastline · Made with Natural Earth
The Pacific continues across the two edges of this map.

narration.en: The land on the Earth is divided into very large pieces called continents.
Here they are, one by one: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia.
There are seven continents. Asia is the largest, and we live in Asia.
Read this world map with north at the top. Start with North America and South America. Then find Europe and Africa, cross to Asia and Australia, and end at Antarctica along the bottom.

Across the left and right edges of this map is the Pacific Ocean. The Atlantic Ocean is between the Americas and Europe and Africa. Find the Indian Ocean and Arctic Ocean. The Southern Ocean surrounds Antarctica.
The Pacific appears on both edges because the world map cuts the view at one meridian. Imagine rolling up the map so its left and right edges meet. Those Pacific waters are part of the same ocean.
Use the continents around point P to work out which ocean it marks.

explanation.en: Point P is south of Asia and between Africa and Australia. That places it in the Indian Ocean.

whyWrong.en: The Atlantic lies between the Americas and Europe and Africa.
The Pacific is mainly shown near the left and right edges of this map.
